response: Follow-up recommendations for abnormal Papanicolaou smears do not significantly influence patient adherence. According to the available data, adherence to follow-up was low in a family planning clinic population, regardless of the type of follow-up advised. However, the use of up to 3 reminders was found to improve adherence. This suggests that allocating resources to effective methods for improving adherence to follow-up of abnormal results may be more important than the specific follow-up procedure recommended.
